decisive_items: an abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure
an abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship, with the vein coursing to the left of the artery
The third portion of the duodenum was not seen in its expected location
response.rationale: R5 uniquely integrates the specific CT triad of malrotation: low transverse colon/right colic flexure, non-visualized D3, and inverted SMA-SMV relationship. R2 uses clustered loops and mesenteric congestion but is weakened by 'no signs of ischemia' and lacks the malrotation-specific anatomy; R4 has only clustered loops; R3 is directly contradicted by a normal appendix; R1 has only nonspecific postprandial discomfort.

rejected.why: Directly contradicted by 'The appendix appeared normal'; McBurney sign and leukocytosis are nonspecific and explained by malrotation-related pain.
Only 'small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right' is supportive; no hernia defect, no surgery history, and it does not explain SMA-SMV inversion or duodenal/colonic malposition.
Only 'occasional postprandial abdominal discomfort' is nonspecific; no imaging evidence of bowel wall inflammation, strictures, or chronic inflammatory changes.
